predecessors.name: Lan Na Kingdom
predecessors.text: the part of Lan Na's 1362 shape inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape ('some of its territory', the Chiang Saen and Mekong lands)

predecessors.name: Khmer Empire
predecessors.text: the northern Khmer lands (Isan north of the Mun and the Mekong valley), as Cliopatria draws their passage to Lan Xang

predecessors.name: Đại Việt (Ngô to Hồ dynasties)
predecessors.text: the western uplands of the 1362 Đại Việt shape that lie inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape ('Xam Neua and several smaller Đại Việt towns')

predecessors.name: Sukhothai Kingdom
predecessors.text: Muang Sua (Luang Prabang) and Vieng Chan (Vientiane), tributaries of Sukhothai in Cliopatria's 1294-1362 shapes

successors.name: Kingdom of Luang Phrabang
successors.text: Luang Prabang, where Kitsarat's coronation in 1707 created the Kingdom of Luang Prabang

successors.name: Kingdom of Vientiane
successors.text: Vientiane and the centre, 'converting Lan Xang into the Kingdom of Vientiane'

successors.name: Kingdom of Champasak
successors.text: the southern part of Lan Xang, which seceded

rulers.name: Voravongsa I (Maha Oupahat, Chao Tha Heua)

ledger.x: 1353: Fa Ngum is crowned and founds Lan Xang Hom Khao at Luang Prabang.
1353: Fa Ngum defeats Lan Na at Chiang Saen.
1363: the Khorat Plateau comes into the Lan Xang outline.
1363: Xam Neua and the Đại Việt border towns join the outline.
1471: Dai Viet claims Muang Phuan (Xiang Khouang) inside Lan Xang.
1479: Lê Thánh Tông takes Luang Prabang.
November 1484: the Dai Viet forces are gone and Muang Phuan is Lan Xang's again.
1546: Prince Xaysettha of Lan Xang is crowned King of Lan Na.
1551: the Lan Na nobles choose Mekuti.
1560: Setthathirath formally moves the capital of Lan Xang from Luang Prabang to Vientiane.
February 1570: Bayinnaung's second army drives Setthathirath from Vientiane.
6 December 1574: the Burmese king and his armies enter Vientiane.
16 April 1575: the Burmese king returns to Pegu.
1707: Kitsarat's coronation at Luang Prabang splits the kingdom.
1707: Lan Xang ends, divided between Luang Prabang and Vientiane.

wars.name: Fa Ngum's conquests
wars.outcome: Fa Ngum took Muang Phuan, Xiang Khouang, Muang Sua and Vientiane, crossed the Khorat Plateau to Roi Et and defeated King Phayu of Lan Na at Chiang Saen, which 'forced Lanna to cede some its territory'.

wars.name: Đại Việt invasion of Lan Xang
wars.outcome: Lê Thánh Tông's army of 180,000 captured Luang Phabang and killed the ruler Chakkaphat; Suvanna Balang was crowned in 1479 and Lan Xang kept its territory.

wars.name: Lan Xang-Ayutthaya war of 1540
wars.outcome: Lan Xang 'defeated an Ayutthaya invasion at Sala Kham in 1540'; a treaty of 1563 sealed by a betrothal followed, and no border moved.

wars.name: Lan Xang-Lan Na campaigns of 1553-1555
wars.outcome: 'In 1553 King Setthathirath sent an army to retake Lanna from Mekuti but was defeated'; in 1555 he 'managed to take Chiang Saen'.

wars.name: Burmese invasions of Lan Xang
wars.outcome: Vientiane taken 2 January 1565 and left 1 August 1565; retaken by Setthathirath in 1568; second invasion October 1569-April 1570; after Setthathirath's death Sen Soulintha resisted until the Burmese entered Vientiane on 6 December 1574; Bayinnaung left on 16…

wars.name: Lao invasions of Cambodia
wars.outcome: 'The Khmer Chronicles record that armies from Lan Xang invaded in 1571 and 1572'; the Khmer king was slain in the second invasion and Lan Xang retreated.

wars.name: Lan Xang civil war and end of Burmese suzerainty
wars.outcome: 'From 1583 to 1591 a civil war took place in Lan Xang'; Nokeo Koumane 'was crowned in Vientiane' in 1591, marched to Luang Prabang and 'cast off any allegiance to the Toungoo Empire'.

certainty.note: No page gives a surveyed or treaty frontier.
